summary: A list of tasks an agent runs on a schedule, like a weekly design QA. Each row says its schedule in words, when it runs next and how its last run went, with Run now and an on/off switch. A run whose last attempt failed says why and can offer a fix, a paused one dims and says Paused, and New schedule makes another from Every day, Every Monday or Custom days.
use: When people set an agent to repeat work, like checking pages every week or syncing tokens every morning.
When people need to see at a glance which recurring runs passed and which failed.
When a run fails for a reason people can fix, like an expired token, and should run again once it is fixed.
When people want to pause a recurring run without deleting it.
features: Each run in `runs` shows its `name`, its `schedule` in words with its `next` run, and its last `result`: "Passed 5 days ago", "Failed: Figma token expired", "Running now" or "No runs yet".

The result leads with its mark: a green tick when it passed, a red sign when it failed, and a turning ring while it runs, when its words shimmer. Its tile shows a service logo (`brand`) on white, or an `icon` on a vivid tile of its `color`; in Clean the tiles are one neutral grey.
`onRunNow` adds Run now to each row, a labelled ghost button just before the switch, so the switch is the one control on the row's right edge; it is unavailable while the run is running or paused.
The switch pauses and resumes a run (`enabled`), and the change comes back through `onRunsChange`. A paused row dims and reads "Paused" in place of its next run.
A failed run with a `fix` shows a button with that label that calls `onFix`; set `fixing` to spin it. The button is as wide as its words and eases to "Reconnecting" and back.

`onCreate` adds New schedule: a form with the task, Every day, Every Monday or Custom days, and a line saying when the first run would be. Create hands over the task, the days, the schedule in words and when it runs next. The form opens under the button, or above it when there is no room below.
`status` adds a line under the title, like "Next run in 17h". Without it the head is the title alone, since the rows already say which runs are on, paused or failed.
The card grows and shrinks with its rows, eased, and keeps no room for a state still to come.
a11y: The runs form a list. Each Run now button is named for its run, like "Run Weekly design QA now".
Each switch has role="switch" and aria-checked, is named for its run, and has a Pause or Resume tooltip.

New schedule opens a dialog that grows out of the button and goes back into it as it closes; its Repeat options are a labelled group of pressed buttons, and the Custom days are buttons named in full, like "Wednesday".
With reduced motion, rows appear without their entrance and text changes without the crossfade.

faq.q: Does Run now start the run?
faq.a: No. It calls `onRunNow` with the run's key. Start it in your own code, set its `result` to 'running', and to 'passed' or 'failed' when it ends.

faq.q: How do I show a fix like reconnecting a service?
faq.a: Give the failed run a `fix` label, like "Reconnect Figma". When `onFix` is called, set `fixing` while you reconnect, then run it again and update its `result`.

faq.q: What time do new schedules run at?
faq.a: At `time`, 9:00 unless you change it, with `hour` set to match so the form can say when the first run is. The days come back as numbers, 0 for Monday to 6 for Sunday.

faq.q: Can I write schedules my own way?
faq.a: Yes. `schedule` and `next` are plain text, so "Weekdays at 8:30" or "Next tomorrow" work as well.

faq.q: What colours can a run's tile take?
faq.a: Any colour in `color`. One of the avatar colours, like 'var(--dm-av-l)', gives the icon that colour's own ink; any other colour gives it white. A `brand` logo sits on a white tile instead.
